how.en: A text says a parcel is waiting and asks you to confirm your details or pay a small fee through a link. The link goes to a fake courier page that collects your personal and card details. Real couriers don’t ask you to confirm details through random links.

text.en: A text from a courier says your parcel can’t be delivered.
It asks you to confirm your details through a link.
The page asks for a small fee and your card details.
UPS: Your package is on hold at our Malta depot due to an incomplete address. Update your details and pay the €1.99 handling charge today: [link]

en: confirm my address for a parcel
small fee to deliver the parcel
package on hold at the depot
A text about a parcel you weren’t expecting.
A delivery fee paid through a link.
A web address that is not the courier’s real one.
Don’t open the link. Check tracking on the courier’s own website or app.
If you entered card details, call your bank.
Report the text to the Police Cyber Crime Unit.

sources.title: Police issue warning on text message parcel scam
